events.title: Accession of Queen Elizabeth II
events.description: Upon the death of her father King George VI at Sandringham House, Princess Elizabeth became Queen of the United Kingdom and the other Commonwealth realms. She was in Kenya at the time and returned to Britain as monarch. Her coronation followed in June 1953.
events.significance: Began a 70-year reign, the longest in British history, during which the Commonwealth evolved and the monarchy adapted to the modern era.

events.title: Massachusetts Ratifies the U.S. Constitution
events.description: Massachusetts voted 187 to 168 to ratify the United States Constitution, becoming the sixth state to do so. Ratification came with a recommended list of proposed amendments.
events.significance: The recommended amendments set a precedent that helped lead to the Bill of Rights, easing ratification in other states.

events.title: Birth of Ronald Reagan
events.description: Ronald Wilson Reagan was born in Tampico, Illinois. He worked as an actor and union leader, served as Governor of California from 1967 to 1975, and was elected the 40th President of the United States in 1980.
events.significance: His presidency (1981-1989) reshaped American conservatism, brought major tax and economic policy changes, and coincided with the late Cold War and its thaw with the Soviet Union.

events.title: Representation of the People Act Grants Votes to Some British Women
events.description: The Representation of the People Act 1918 received royal assent, giving the vote to all men over 21 and to women over 30 who met property qualifications. It greatly expanded the British electorate.
events.significance: A landmark in the women's suffrage movement in Britain, paving the way for equal voting rights for women in 1928.

events.title: Munich Air Disaster
events.description: A plane carrying the Manchester United football team crashed on takeoff at Munich-Riem airport after a refueling stop, killing 23 of the 44 on board, including eight players known as the 'Busby Babes'.
events.significance: One of the most tragic events in sports history; Manchester United later rebuilt under Matt Busby and won the European Cup in 1968.
